issue.title: bug: Vibe doesn't know today's date

steps: What is today's date? Answer with the exact calendar date.
expected: The agent should receive the actual current calendar date in its system context and answer that date without requiring the user to supply it.
defect: The tested version omits the current date from system context. In the fresh original ABB execution the model answered 2024-06-14 although the actual test date was 2026-10-26.

fault location.explanation: Original model requests omit current-date context. Adding the dynamically computed date here makes it appear in actual requests and changes the answer to the actual test date.
The template lacks a current-date placeholder. This is supporting context; the tested patch injects the date in get_universal_system_prompt without editing this template.

Root cause: CONFIRMED BY SOURCE, ACTUAL MODEL REQUESTS AND A FRESH ABB BEFORE/AFTER COMPARISON AT v2.10.1. get_universal_system_prompt assembles instructions without injecting the current calendar date; the CLI template also lacks a date placeholder. The original outgoing system context contained no current-date line, and the model answered 2024-06-14. A minimal candidate patch adds a dynamically computed date.today().isoformat() line to the assembled instructions. On the actual test date, 2026-10-26, the patched outgoing system context included 'Today's date is 2026-10-26.' and the model answered 2026-10-26. Neither arm called a date tool, and the user prompt and model configuration were unchanged. Separate source-function controls with simulated dates 2024-02-29 and 2030-01-02 confirmed that the patch derives the date at runtime rather than hardcoding the successful answer. These results validate the missing-context fault and candidate repair. fixed_in=2.11.0 records the previously established upstream date-injection release, not a release tested in this repair experiment. pinned_contains_fix=false refers to the unmodified tested v2.10.1 commit. The earlier reported version was 2.7.2. Correct answers remain model-dependent; a model could also obtain the date through a tool without this repair.
